BLI 0515 is the APN procurement line whose own title and narrative name is 'Infrared Search and Track (IRST)' — the same appropriation colour as the award (APN), and the same hardware (IRST receiver/processor sets built by Lockheed Martin Orlando). This is end-item procurement of the IRST line's own hardware, not sustainment or platform support: the aircraft is named only to identify which IRST variant. The competing owner of the name (0604014N, the RDT&E line) is refuted by money colour — an APN hardware buy does not execute an RDT&E PE — and is proposed separately as wrong so the collision is on the record.

refute_a.reason: Money: the award obligates FY2019 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds, but LI 0515's own APN narrative (doc 330) says the line "was established in FY2021" and that IRST/OSIP 04-14 "can be found in LI-0525 for FY20 and prior" — and the warehouse carries no APN IRST line before FY2021 (only the "F-18 Series" modification line) — so this FY2019 APN money executed on a different line item, not this one.

refute_b.reason: A different PE owns the announcement's own words: index row 'F/A-18 Infrared Search and Track (IRST)' belongs to 0604014N (doc 340), whose AN/ASG-34A narrative calls it 'the AN/ASG-34A(V)1 F/A-18E/F Infrared Search and Track (IRST) system' — the evidence string 'the F/A-18 Infrared Search and Track System' matches that row more literally than 0515's bare title, and the announcement carries no identity cue (no receiver/processor designator, no in-service vs development marker) that picks 0515 over it; only appropriation colour separates them, which is lens A's ground, not identity.
